M5 Slice 5 — the event explorer. This is the last thing M5 owed (§19: "…menu management + events, event explorer, hide/unhide…"; §11.4: "filter security/order/menu events by subject, actor, type, and time").

Files to delete: none. No migration, no packages, no schema change. 15 files: 7 new, 8 edited, all additive.

Edited — Program.cs (one using, one call), the five administration headers (one <a> each), and OrderTestWorld.cs (two writers). Full diff-level detail is in _CHANGES.md.

Three things worth flagging before you build:

Program.cs was edited, for the first time since M4 Slice 1. The four existing extensions stay welded together because omitting a piece is a silent half-failure. The explorer isn't like that — it reads identity's audit log, ordering's, and the menu's, so folding it into AddRestaurantOrders() would make the orders extension the registrar of a security_event reader, and omitting it throws loudly on one route rather than half-working everywhere.

The security branch's LEFT JOIN is the load-bearing line. security_event.actor_person_identifier is the only nullable actor column in the three tables. An INNER there compiles, runs, returns rows, and silently hides every lockout and failed sign-in from the one screen built to find them.

Likeliest compiler catch: EventExplorer.razor, and specifically [SupplyParameterFromQuery(Name = …)] private string[]? Streams { get; set; } — the first array-valued query parameter in the tree. <fieldset>/<optgroup> and class="event-stream-@entry.Stream" are also firsts here. Every <text> block sits inside an @if body; the one markup-context separator is a <span>, mirroring HiddenRecords.

Expect +49 facts. With M5 Slice 4's projected 877 as baseline: 926 total, 911 passing, 15 skipped.

With this, M5 is closed. M6 is hardening — the Playwright matrix, the restore drill, and CI.
